title: Resolve a next_id-only merge conflict without hand-editing the index
lead: The `next_id` counter in `.slicer/index.json` is a single line that every filing changes. Two branches that each file anything conflict on it at merge time, even when their new ids differ, and the only fix today is a hand edit of tracking JSON, which the project's own rules forbid.
findings_note: merging s174 into a main whose next_id had moved conflicted only on next_id; resolving it needed a hand edit of index.json
boundary: **Not in this slice:** allocating ids above a sibling worktree's (that is s185); a renumber command; merging any other tracking file; resolving conflicts in a slice file or the log.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Hit twice in two days. On 2026-10-04 two filing branches clashed on ids. On 2026-10-05, s174 merged into a `main` that had moved from `next_id` 186 to 189; the one conflict hunk was `"next_id": 189` against `188`, and resolving it took a hand edit of `index.json`. The right answer is always the larger value, so ids are never reused. `slicer setup-git` already installs a merge driver for generated render files, so the project has a place for another one. s185 stops two checkouts allocating the same id; it does not touch this conflict, which remains after s185 because the two branches still add different items.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` (a hidden `merge-index` subcommand)
- `src/slicer/vcs.py` (allow `git merge-file`, and `setup-git` wiring)
- `src/slicer/store.py` or a new small module for the merge rule
- `docs/commands.md`, `docs/agents.md`
- `tests/test_cli.py` or a new `tests/test_merge_index.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. Given a base, ours and theirs index where only `next_id` differs on both sides, `slicer merge-index BASE OURS THEIRS` writes OURS with the larger `next_id` and exits 0.
2. Given two sides that also differ elsewhere without overlapping, the result keeps both changes and the larger `next_id`.
3. Given overlapping edits to the same item, or conflicts beyond `next_id`, it exits non-zero and leaves the usual conflict markers, so Git reports a normal conflict.
4. `slicer setup-git` configures the driver for `.slicer/index.json` and is idempotent. `slicer check` or `verify` warns when the driver is missing, as it does for the render driver.
5. In a scratch repo, merging two branches that each `add` an item completes with no conflict and `slicer check` is clean afterwards.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Add the driver and have `setup-git` register it in the repository's Git config and attributes, next to the existing render driver. The driver runs a three-way merge of the file and, when the only remaining conflict is the `next_id` line, resolves it to the larger number. Anything else stays a normal conflict.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
